themes.title: Sons of Jacob
themes.clue: Brothers whose names became tribal names
themes.explain: Jacob, renamed Israel, had twelve sons by Leah, Rachel, Bilhah and Zilpah, and their families became the twelve tribes. Jesus chose twelve apostles to signal the gathering of a renewed Israel, the Church.

themes.title: Sons of Leah
themes.clue: Six brothers born to the unloved wife
themes.explain: Leah, less loved than her sister Rachel, bore Jacob six sons; the LORD 'saw that Leah was hated' and blessed her. From her came both the priestly tribe of Levi and the royal tribe of Judah, from which the Messiah was born.

themes.title: Mothers of the Twelve Tribes
themes.clue: Two sisters and their two maidservants
themes.explain: Jacob's twelve sons were born of four women: the sisters Leah and Rachel and their maids Bilhah and Zilpah. Ruth 4:11 remembers Rachel and Leah as the two who 'built the house of Israel.'

themes.title: On the Ark
themes.clue: A father and the three sons through whom the earth was repopulated
themes.explain: Noah, his three sons and their wives (eight souls) were saved through water. St Peter sees here a figure of Baptism, and the Fathers saw the ark as the Church, outside which the world was lost (1 Pet 3:20-21; CCC 845, 1219).

themes.title: The First Family
themes.clue: Eden's parents and their sons
themes.explain: Adam and Eve were the first parents; their sons Cain and Abel gave us the first murder, and Seth was given 'instead of Abel.' The Church calls Christ the New Adam and Mary the New Eve.

themes.title: Before the Flood
themes.clue: Long-lived generations from Adam's third son down to the ark-builder
themes.explain: Genesis 5 traces the godly line of Seth, in whose days people 'began to call on the LORD's name,' down to Noah. Luke's genealogy runs through these same names back to Adam, 'the son of God.'

themes.title: Abraham's Household
themes.clue: The wives, sons and nephew of the father of faith
themes.explain: Abraham's family included Sarah, mother of the promised son Isaac; Hagar, mother of Ishmael; Keturah, his later wife; and his nephew Lot. The Church calls Abraham 'our father in faith' (Roman Canon; CCC 145-146).

themes.title: Sons of Aaron
themes.clue: Four brothers anointed with their father; two died offering strange fire
themes.explain: Aaron's four sons were consecrated priests with him; Nadab and Abihu died for offering 'strange fire,' and the priesthood passed through Eleazar and Ithamar. Israel's priesthood foreshadows the one priesthood of Christ (CCC 1539-1545).

themes.title: Clans of Levi
themes.clue: A patriarch and the three sons whose clans carried the tabernacle
themes.explain: Levi's sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari headed the Levite clans, each charged with carrying part of the tabernacle. Moses and Aaron themselves descended from Kohath.

themes.title: Family of Moses
themes.clue: His parents, siblings, wife and firstborn
themes.explain: Moses was born to Amram and Jochebed of the house of Levi, with Aaron and Miriam as siblings; he married Zipporah of Midian, who bore Gershom and Eliezer. God worked through a whole family, not a lone hero.

themes.title: Sons of Zeruiah
themes.clue: David's sister and her three warrior sons
themes.explain: Zeruiah's sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel were David's nephews and fiercest captains, so hard-handed that David said, 'These men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me.'

themes.title: Sons of Jesse
themes.clue: Brothers passed over before the youngest was anointed
themes.explain: Samuel looked at Jesse's tall elder sons, but the LORD said, 'Man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart,' and chose the youngest, David. Isaiah foretold a shoot from the stump of Jesse: the Messiah.

themes.title: David's Wives
themes.clue: Women married to Israel's shepherd king
themes.explain: David married Saul's daughter Michal, wise Abigail, Ahinoam, Haggith and others, and later Bathsheba after his grave sin. Bathsheba, mother of Solomon, is named in Matthew's genealogy as 'her who had been Uriah's wife.'

themes.title: Sons of David
themes.clue: Princes born at Hebron and Jerusalem
themes.explain: Of David's sons, Amnon was killed by Absalom, Absalom rebelled, Adonijah grasped at the throne, and Solomon was chosen to reign. God's promise that David's son would rule forever is fulfilled in Jesus, 'Son of David.'

themes.title: House of Saul
themes.clue: The first king's father, children, cousin and concubine
themes.explain: Saul was the son of Kish; his children included Jonathan, David's covenant friend, and the daughters Merab and Michal. Abner, his cousin, commanded his army, and Rizpah's vigil over her slain sons is one of Scripture's great pictures of a mother's grief.

themes.title: Josiah's Sons
themes.clue: Three of them wore the crown as Judah collapsed
themes.explain: Good King Josiah was followed by three sons, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, none of whom kept his reform; the firstborn Johanan never reigned. Their failure ended with the Babylonian exile.

themes.title: Sons of Mattathias
themes.clue: Five priestly brothers who led the revolt
themes.explain: When Antiochus IV outlawed the Law, the priest Mattathias and his five sons rose up; Judas 'the Maccabee' rededicated the Temple, and Jonathan and Simon later led as high priests. Their fidelity unto death is honored in the Church's Old Testament canon.

themes.title: Brethren of the Lord
themes.clue: Four men the people of Nazareth named as Jesus' 'brothers'
themes.explain: Nazareth's townsfolk named James, Joses, Simon and Judas as Jesus' 'brothers.' The Church teaches these were close relatives, not other children of Mary, who remained ever-virgin; Joses and James are elsewhere sons of another Mary (CCC 500).

themes.title: The Holy Family
themes.clue: Nazareth's household, with grandparents from Tradition
themes.explain: Jesus grew up in the home of Mary and Joseph at Nazareth, 'subject to them.' Tradition (not Scripture) names Mary's parents Joachim and Anne, honored together on July 26.

themes.title: At Bethany
themes.clue: Friends whose home Jesus loved to visit
themes.explain: Jesus loved Martha, Mary and their brother Lazarus, whom he raised from the dead; he was also anointed at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper. The Church keeps Martha, Mary and Lazarus together on July 29.

themes.title: Daughters of Zelophehad
themes.clue: Five sisters who asked Moses for their father's land
themes.explain: Zelophehad died with no sons, so his five daughters petitioned Moses for an inheritance, and the LORD said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right.' Yes, one of them was named Noah.

themes.title: Sons of Anak
themes.clue: The tall clan of Hebron that frightened the spies
themes.explain: At Hebron the twelve spies saw Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the children of Anak, and ten spies lost heart. Caleb, trusting the LORD, later drove them out (Josh 15:14).

themes.title: Esau's Family
themes.clue: The red twin, a wife and the chiefs of Edom
themes.explain: Esau, also called Edom, married Canaanite and Ishmaelite wives; his sons Eliphaz and Reuel headed the chiefs of Edom. Israel was told, 'You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother.'

themes.title: Judges of Israel
themes.clue: Deliverers raised up between Joshua and the kings
themes.explain: When Israel fell into idolatry and was oppressed, 'the LORD raised up judges, who saved them.' The cycle of sin, suffering, repentance and rescue shows God's patience with his people.

themes.title: The Minor Judges
themes.clue: Judges remembered in only a verse or two
themes.explain: Shamgar, Tola, Jair, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon judged Israel with few recorded deeds, often noted only for sons, donkeys or burial places. Faithful, hidden service counts in God's history too.

themes.title: Victory over Sisera
themes.clue: A prophetess, a general, a tent-dweller and two Canaanites
themes.explain: Deborah summoned Barak against Jabin's general Sisera; the LORD routed Sisera's chariots, and Jael killed him in her tent. Deborah's song calls Jael 'blessed above women,' words echoed when Elizabeth greets Mary as 'blessed among women.'

themes.title: Gideon and Midian
themes.clue: A judge with 300 men and the princes and kings he defeated
themes.explain: With only 300 men, Gideon routed Midian; the princes Oreb and Zeeb and the kings Zebah and Zalmunna were captured and slain. Psalm 83 later prays that God's enemies be treated 'like Oreb and Zeeb.'

themes.title: Major Prophets
themes.clue: The four long prophetic books
themes.explain: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel are called 'major' prophets for the length of their books, not their importance; in the Catholic Bible Lamentations and Baruch accompany Jeremiah. Isaiah is read so often in Advent he is called the 'fifth evangelist.'

themes.title: The Twelve
themes.clue: Shorter prophetic books, gathered as one scroll
themes.explain: The twelve 'minor' prophets, Hosea through Malachi, were kept on one scroll; Sirach prays, 'May the bones of the twelve prophets flourish.' Their shortness hides great themes: Hosea's faithful love, Amos's justice, Jonah's sign.

themes.title: Seers
themes.clue: Prophets given the older title for 'one who sees'
themes.explain: 'He who is now called a prophet was before called a seer.' Samuel, Gad, Iddo and Hanani are each called 'the seer,' and Chronicles cites their records of the kings.

themes.title: Prophetesses
themes.clue: Women Scripture calls prophets
themes.explain: Miriam led Israel's song at the sea, Deborah judged Israel, Huldah confirmed the rediscovered Law to Josiah, and Anna spoke of the infant Jesus in the Temple. All four are explicitly called prophetesses.

themes.title: Prophets Without Books
themes.clue: Prophets of the kings' era who left no book of their own
themes.explain: Many prophets spoke God's word to kings without leaving a book: Nathan rebuked David, Ahijah tore his cloak into twelve pieces before Jeroboam, Micaiah alone told Ahab the truth, and Elijah and Elisha confronted Baal worship.

themes.title: Apostles
themes.clue: Men Jesus called and sent
themes.explain: Jesus chose Twelve to be with him and to be sent out, with Peter at their head; the bishops are their successors (CCC 860-862). Their number recalls the twelve tribes of Israel.

themes.title: Fishermen of Galilee
themes.clue: They left their nets to follow
themes.explain: Jesus called the brothers Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John, who left their father Zebedee in the boat: 'Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.'

themes.title: The Four Evangelists
themes.clue: Authors of the Gospels
themes.explain: The Church receives four Gospels, by Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, as the heart of all Scripture because they are our principal source for the life and teaching of the Word made flesh (CCC 125-127).

themes.title: The Seven
themes.clue: Men chosen to serve tables so the apostles could pray and preach
themes.explain: The apostles laid hands on seven men 'of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom' to serve the Hellenist widows. The Church sees here the origin of the diaconate; Stephen became the first martyr.

themes.title: High Priests
themes.clue: Holders of Israel's highest priestly office, from Sinai to the Passion
themes.explain: Aaron was the first high priest, followed by Eleazar; Zadok served under David and Solomon, Hilkiah found the Book of the Law, and Annas and Caiaphas presided at Jesus' trial. Hebrews shows Christ as the high priest who offered himself once for all.

themes.title: High Priests in Crisis
themes.clue: One faithful priest and three who bought or seized the office
themes.explain: Under the Seleucids the high priesthood was corrupted: the pious Onias was ousted by his brother Jason, who was outbid by Menelaus; later Alcimus was installed by Demetrius. 2 Maccabees shows how faithless shepherds scatter the flock.

themes.title: Kings of Judah
themes.clue: Sons of David who reigned in Jerusalem after the split
themes.explain: After Solomon the kingdom split, and David's descendants reigned in Judah; Matthew's genealogy runs through these very kings to Jesus, the Son of David whose kingdom has no end.

themes.title: Kings of the North
themes.clue: Rulers of the ten tribes from Samaria
themes.explain: The northern kingdom of Israel had no king who fully turned from Jeroboam's golden calves; dynasties fell by assassination until Assyria took Samaria under Hoshea in 722 BC.

themes.title: Anointed Kings
themes.clue: Rulers on whose heads holy oil was poured
themes.explain: Samuel anointed Saul and David, Zadok anointed Solomon, and a son of the prophets anointed Jehu. 'Messiah' and 'Christ' both mean 'Anointed One': Jesus is the King all these anointings pointed to (CCC 436).

themes.title: Queen Mothers
themes.clue: Women named beside their royal sons in the book of Kings
themes.explain: Judah's kings are introduced with their mothers' names, because the queen mother (gebirah) held an honored office; Solomon set a throne for Bathsheba at his right hand. The Church sees here a figure of Mary, Queen Mother of the Son of David.

themes.title: The Herodian Family
themes.clue: A ruling family that met Jesus, John and Paul
themes.explain: Herod the Great's family ruled under Rome: Archelaus in Judea, Antipas in Galilee (who beheaded John), and later Agrippa II, who heard Paul's defense with his sister Bernice. Herodias pressed for John's death.

themes.title: Roman Governors
themes.clue: Officials who ruled provinces for Caesar
themes.explain: Quirinius governed Syria at the census, Pilate condemned Jesus, Sergius Paulus believed at Paphos, Gallio dismissed charges against Paul, and Felix and Festus kept him in custody. The Creed names Pilate to anchor our faith in real history.

themes.title: Kings of the Nations
themes.clue: Rulers of Persia, Tyre, Egypt and the Amorites
themes.explain: God's purposes ran through pagan kings too: Hiram supplied cedar for the Temple, Shishak plundered it, Necoh killed Josiah, Sihon blocked the Exodus, and Cyrus and Darius allowed the Temple to be rebuilt. Isaiah even calls Cyrus the LORD's 'anointed.'

themes.title: Philistines
themes.clue: Rulers and champions of the coastal enemy
themes.explain: Abimelech of Gerar and his captain Phicol made covenants with Abraham and Isaac; Goliath of Gath defied Israel's armies; and David later took refuge with Achish, king of Gath.

themes.title: Moabites
themes.clue: People from beyond the Dead Sea, one of them David's great-grandmother
themes.explain: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, Eglon was slain by Ehud, and Mesha rebelled after Ahab's death. Yet the Moabitess Ruth became David's great-grandmother and an ancestor of Christ, a sign that salvation is for all nations.

themes.title: Midianites
themes.clue: Moses' in-laws and others from the desert people
themes.explain: Moses married Zipporah, daughter of the Midianite priest Jethro, and asked her brother Hobab to guide Israel; but at Peor the Midianite Cozbi led Israel into sin. Midian is both kin and adversary in the Exodus story.

themes.title: David's Court
themes.clue: Commander, chief guard, two priests, a prophet and a counselor
themes.explain: David ruled with Joab over the army, Benaiah over the bodyguard, Zadok and Abiathar as priests, Nathan as prophet and Hushai as loyal friend and counselor. Even the best king needed others, including a prophet willing to rebuke him.

themes.title: David's Mighty Men
themes.clue: Heroes listed among 'the three' and 'the thirty'
themes.explain: 2 Samuel 23 lists David's champions: Abishai, chief of the three, Benaiah, who killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day, Asahel, and Uriah the Hittite, whose loyalty shamed the king who wronged him.

themes.title: Psalmists
themes.clue: Singers named in the Psalter's headings
themes.explain: David appointed Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun to 'prophesy with harps,' and their names head psalms the Church still prays daily in the Liturgy of the Hours. Christ himself prayed the Psalms on the cross.

themes.title: Sages of the Wisdom Books
themes.clue: A famous king and three lesser-known teachers of wisdom
themes.explain: Proverbs is attributed to Solomon with chapters by Agur and King Lemuel (taught by his mother), and Sirach was written by Jesus son of Sirach. The Church reads these books as inspired guides to living in the fear of the Lord.

themes.title: Book of Tobit
themes.clue: A blind father, a son on a journey, a bride and a disguised guide
themes.explain: Tobit, blinded while doing works of mercy, sends his son Tobias on a journey guided by the archangel Raphael, who heals Tobit and frees Sarah from a demon. The Church reads Tobit at weddings and honors Raphael on September 29.

themes.title: Tobit's Kin and Companions
themes.clue: Relatives at Ecbatana and Rages, plus an angel
themes.explain: Tobias journeyed with Raphael to recover silver left with Gabael and found a wife in Sarah, daughter of Raguel and Edna. God's providence works quietly through family, hospitality and an angel's guidance.

themes.title: Book of Judith
themes.clue: A widow, an Ammonite who believed, a eunuch, a priest and a Median king
themes.explain: Judith, a devout widow of Bethulia, saved her people from Holofernes; the Ammonite Achior foretold Israel's protection and believed, Bagoas found his master dead, and the high priest Joakim blessed her: 'You are the great glory of Israel!' The Church applies this praise to Mary.

themes.title: Feast of Purim
themes.clue: A queen, her guardian, a villain, his wife, a deposed queen and a chamberlain
themes.explain: Vashti was deposed, Esther became queen under Hegai's care, and with Mordecai she foiled Haman's plot, prompted by his wife Zeresh, to destroy the Jews. The Catholic Esther includes Esther's prayer, and the Church sees Mary's intercession foreshadowed in hers.

themes.title: Story of Susanna
themes.clue: A chaste wife, her husband, her father and her young defender
themes.explain: Susanna, wife of Joakim and daughter of Helkias, chose death rather than sin, and young Daniel exposed the two lying elders by questioning them apart. Daniel 13 is part of the Catholic canon and is read in Lent.

themes.title: Foes of Judas Maccabeus
themes.clue: A persecuting king and three of his commanders
themes.explain: Antiochus IV profaned the Temple; his generals Lysias, Gorgias and Nicanor were defeated by Judas Maccabeus, whose victory over Nicanor was kept as a feast. Judas reminded his men that the enemy trusted in weapons, but Israel in the Almighty God.

themes.title: Maccabean Martyrs
themes.clue: An aged scribe, a widow with seven sons, and an elder of Jerusalem
themes.explain: Under Antiochus IV the ninety-year-old Eleazar, a mother and her seven sons, and the elder Razis chose death rather than betray the Law or fall into the persecutors' hands. The mother's words to her sons are a key Old Testament witness to creation from nothing and the resurrection of the body (CCC 297, 992).

themes.title: Types of Christ
themes.clue: Old Testament figures in whom the Fathers saw Jesus foreshadowed
themes.explain: Adam is 'a type of him who was to come'; Abel the innocent slain shepherd, Isaac carrying the wood up Moriah, Joseph betrayed and exalted, Moses the lawgiver, and Jonah three days in the fish all prefigure Christ. The New Testament lies hidden in the Old (CCC 128-130).

themes.title: Types of Mary
themes.clue: Women in whom the Church sees the Mother of God foreshadowed
themes.explain: Mary is the New Eve; like Sarah and Hannah she receives a God-given son; like Judith and Esther she stands with her people; and like Bathsheba she is Queen Mother beside the Son of David's throne (CCC 489).

themes.title: Taken Up
themes.clue: Two taken alive, one ascended, one assumed
themes.explain: Enoch 'was not found, for God took him,' and Elijah went up by a whirlwind. Christ ascended by his own power, and Mary was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory, a share in her Son's Resurrection (CCC 659, 966).

themes.title: Given a New Name
themes.clue: Names given by God or by Jesus to mark a new mission
themes.explain: Abram became Abraham, Sarai became Sarah, Jacob became Israel, Hoshea became Joshua, and Simon became Peter (Cephas, 'Rock'). In Scripture a new name means a new identity and calling, as each of us receives a name at Baptism (CCC 2156).

themes.title: Forty Days
themes.clue: Each is linked with a forty-day span in Scripture
themes.explain: Rain fell on Noah forty days, Moses stayed forty days on Sinai, Elijah walked forty days to Horeb, Goliath taunted Israel forty days, and Jesus fasted forty days in the desert. The Church's Lent unites us to these forty days (CCC 540).

themes.title: Raised from Death
themes.clue: Three returned to earthly life; one rose never to die again
themes.explain: Jesus raised Lazarus, Peter raised Tabitha, and Paul revived Eutychus, but they returned to ordinary life and died again. Christ's Resurrection is essentially different: he rose to a glorified life beyond death (CCC 646).

themes.title: Songs of Praise
themes.clue: Each sang or prayed a canticle the Church still uses
themes.explain: Hannah's song, Miriam's song at the sea, Judith's hymn, Zechariah's Benedictus and Simeon's Nunc Dimittis are all prayed in the Liturgy of the Hours, alongside Mary's Magnificat.

themes.title: Here I Am
themes.clue: Each answered God's call with the same three words
themes.explain: Abraham at Moriah, Moses at the bush, the boy Samuel in the night and Isaiah in the Temple all answered, 'Here I am.' Mary's 'Behold, the handmaid of the Lord' is the perfect form of this answer (CCC 2617).

themes.title: Reluctant Servants
themes.clue: Each objected or fled when God called
themes.explain: Moses said he was slow of speech, Gideon that his clan was the weakest, Jeremiah that he was only a youth, and Jonah fled toward Tarshish. God's call does not depend on our feeling ready.

themes.title: Barren Women Who Bore Sons
themes.clue: God opened the womb of each
themes.explain: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah and Elizabeth were barren until God gave them sons. These births prepare for the virginal conception of Jesus, which surpasses all human expectation: 'nothing will be impossible with God' (CCC 489, 497).

themes.title: Matriarchs
themes.clue: Wives of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
themes.explain: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel and Leah are the mothers of Israel. Ruth's blessing asks that she be 'like Rachel and like Leah, which both built the house of Israel.'

themes.title: Women of Faith
themes.clue: Brave and faithful women of the Old Testament
themes.explain: Ruth's loyalty, Naomi's endurance, Miriam's praise, Rahab's courageous faith and Hannah's prayer all shaped salvation history. Hebrews 11 names Rahab among the heroes of faith.

themes.title: Women in Matthew's Genealogy
themes.clue: Five mothers named in the line of Jesus Christ
themes.explain: Matthew names Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, 'the wife of Uriah' and Mary among Jesus' ancestors. Several were foreigners or had irregular stories, showing that God writes salvation through unlikely lives, and leading up to Mary, whose motherhood is wholly new.

themes.title: Widows of Scripture
themes.clue: Each outlived a husband
themes.explain: Naomi and her daughters-in-law Ruth and Orpah were widowed in Moab; Tamar was the widow of Er; Judith and Anna spent their widowhood in prayer and fasting. God is called 'a father of the fatherless and a defender of the widows.'

themes.title: Wicked Royal Women
themes.clue: Each used royal power for evil
themes.explain: Jezebel promoted Baal and had Naboth killed, Athaliah murdered the royal heirs, Maacah was deposed as queen mother for an idol, and Herodias sought John the Baptist's head. Power without God becomes a tool of death.

themes.title: Women Who Followed Jesus
themes.clue: They traveled with him and served from their means
themes.explain: Luke names Mary Magdalene, Joanna and Susanna among women who followed Jesus and provided for him; Salome came to the tomb, and Martha confessed him as the Christ. Mary Magdalene, first witness of the Resurrection, is honored as 'apostle to the apostles.'

themes.title: Women in Paul's Mission
themes.clue: Patrons, hosts and co-workers of the Apostle
themes.explain: Phoebe served the church at Cenchreae, Priscilla taught Apollos, Lydia hosted the church at Philippi, Euodia and Syntyche labored with Paul in the gospel, and Chloe's people reported on Corinth. Women were essential to the first mission.

themes.title: Greeted in Romans 16
themes.clue: Names from Paul's long list of greetings
themes.explain: Paul closes Romans by greeting dozens of believers by name, including Junia, 'notable among the apostles,' Urbanus his fellow worker, the beloved Persis, Tryphosa and Rufus 'chosen in the Lord.' The Church was a family of real names.

themes.title: Paul's Companions
themes.clue: Fellow workers on the Apostle's journeys
themes.explain: Paul never worked alone: Barnabas and Silas traveled with him, Timothy and Titus became bishops entrusted with churches, Luke the 'beloved physician' recorded the journeys, and Tychicus carried his letters.

themes.title: Writers of Epistles
themes.clue: Apostolic authors of New Testament letters
themes.explain: The New Testament letters bear the names of Paul, Peter, James, John and Jude. Catholic liturgy honors the Letter of Jude under St Jude the apostle and the Letter of James under St James, 'brother of the Lord.'

themes.title: Converts in Acts
themes.clue: Gentiles and Jews who came to faith through the apostles
themes.explain: Cornelius the centurion received the Spirit at Peter's preaching, Lydia opened her heart at Philippi, Dionysius and Damaris believed at Athens, and Crispus, a synagogue ruler, believed in Corinth. The gospel crossed every boundary.

themes.title: Good Friday
themes.clue: Figures in the arrest and trial of Jesus
themes.explain: Jesus was arrested (Peter cut off Malchus's ear), questioned by Annas and Caiaphas, and handed to Pilate, who released Barabbas instead. The Church teaches that all sinners, not one people, bear responsibility for Christ's Passion (CCC 597-598).

themes.title: At the Cross and Tomb
themes.clue: Those who carried, watched and buried
themes.explain: Simon of Cyrene carried the cross, Mary Magdalene and Salome watched from afar, and Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus wrapped Jesus' body in linen with spices and laid it in a new tomb.

themes.title: Pharisees
themes.clue: Members of the party that most carefully kept the Law
themes.explain: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, Gamaliel counseled the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone, Simon hosted Jesus at dinner, and Paul was 'a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.' Not every Pharisee opposed Jesus.

themes.title: Christmas Story
themes.clue: People in Luke's account of the birth and childhood of Jesus
themes.explain: Gabriel announced the births of John and Jesus, Zechariah and Elizabeth bore the Forerunner, and in the Temple Simeon and Anna recognized the infant Christ. Luke shows faithful Israel welcoming its Messiah.

themes.title: On the Mountain
themes.clue: Three disciples saw their Lord in glory with two visitors
themes.explain: On a high mountain Jesus was transfigured before Peter, James and John, and Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, spoke with him. The feast is kept on August 6 as a foretaste of the Kingdom (CCC 554-556).

themes.title: Martyrs
themes.clue: Each died for fidelity to God
themes.explain: Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the Temple court, the scribe Eleazar died rather than eat pork, Stephen became the first Christian martyr, James was the first apostle martyred, and Antipas was Christ's 'witness, my faithful one' at Pergamum. 'Martyr' means witness (CCC 2473).

themes.title: Shepherds
themes.clue: Each tended flocks
themes.explain: Abel kept sheep, Jacob tended Laban's flocks, Rachel watered her father's sheep, Moses kept Jethro's flock, David was taken from the sheepfold, and Amos was a herdsman of Tekoa. Jesus calls himself the Good Shepherd.

themes.title: They Met an Angel
themes.clue: Each was addressed by a messenger from heaven
themes.explain: An angel found Hagar by a spring, greeted Gideon as a 'mighty man of valor,' announced Samson's birth to Manoah and his wife, guided Tobias, and told Zechariah of John's birth. Angels are servants and messengers of God (CCC 329-333).

themes.title: Angels
themes.clue: Three named archangels and two choirs of heavenly beings
themes.explain: Scripture names three archangels, Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, honored together on September 29, and describes cherubim guarding Eden and seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.' The existence of angels is a truth of faith (CCC 328).

themes.title: Struck with Leprosy
themes.clue: Each was afflicted with a skin disease in the Old Testament
themes.explain: Miriam was struck for speaking against Moses, Naaman was healed after washing in the Jordan, King Uzziah for burning incense he had no right to offer, and Gehazi for his greed. The Fathers saw in Naaman's washing a figure of Baptism.

themes.title: Lost Their Sight
themes.clue: Each was blinded, whether for a time or for good
themes.explain: Tobit was blinded by sparrow droppings, the Philistines put out Samson's eyes, Babylon blinded Zedekiah, Saul was blinded by the light on the Damascus road, and Elymas was struck blind for opposing the gospel. Sight lost and restored often signals conversion.

themes.title: Mountains of Scripture
themes.clue: Peaks where God acted
themes.explain: God gave the Law on Sinai, met Elijah at Horeb, sent fire on Carmel, tested Abraham in the land of Moriah, and chose Zion for his dwelling; Tabor is where Deborah's army gathered and, by Tradition, where Christ was transfigured.

themes.title: Giant Slayers
themes.clue: Each defeated a giant or a giant clan
themes.explain: David killed Goliath, and later his men Abishai, Elhanan and Jonathan son of Shimeah each killed a giant of Gath; Caleb drove the sons of Anak out of Hebron. Faith in God, not size, wins the battle.

themes.title: Builders for God
themes.clue: An ark, a tabernacle, a temple and a city wall
themes.explain: Noah built the ark, Bezalel and Oholiab crafted the tabernacle, Solomon built the Temple with Hiram's bronze work, and Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem's walls. All foreshadow the Church, built of living stones on Christ the cornerstone.

themes.title: Return from Exile
themes.clue: Leaders of the restoration of Jerusalem
themes.explain: After the exile Jeshua the high priest and Zerubbabel rebuilt the altar and Temple, urged on by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah; later Ezra taught the Law and Nehemiah rebuilt the walls.

themes.title: Foes of Jerusalem's Walls
themes.clue: They mocked, plotted against, or halted the rebuilding
themes.explain: Rehum's letter halted work on Jerusalem, and later Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem mocked Nehemiah and plotted to stop him. Nehemiah answered, 'The God of heaven will prosper us.'

themes.title: Exiles in Babylon
themes.clue: Judeans who served God far from home
themes.explain: Daniel and his three companions stayed faithful in Nebuchadnezzar's court, even in the fiery furnace, and Ezekiel prophesied by the river Chebar. The Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three, in the Catholic Daniel 3, are still prayed on Sundays.

themes.title: Dreamers
themes.clue: God or his messenger spoke to each in a dream
themes.explain: Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven, Solomon asked for wisdom in a dream at Gibeon, Pharaoh dreamed of the fat and lean cows, and St Joseph obeyed four dreams protecting Mary and the Child. God guides those who listen.

themes.title: Meetings at a Well
themes.clue: Each found someone, or was found, by water
themes.explain: Abraham's servant found Rebekah at a well, Jacob met Rachel at one, Moses met Zipporah at one, God opened Hagar's eyes to a well, and Jesus met the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well and offered living water.

themes.title: Buried at Machpelah
themes.clue: Laid to rest in the cave bought from Ephron the Hittite
themes.explain: Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah as a burial place; there were buried Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, Leah and Jacob, but not Rachel, who was buried on the road to Bethlehem. Their burial in the promised land was a pledge of faith in God's promise.

themes.title: Firstborn Passed Over
themes.clue: Each was the elder son, yet the blessing went elsewhere
themes.explain: Again and again God chose the younger: Abel's offering over Cain's, Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, Joseph's line over Reuben, Ephraim over Manasseh, and David over Eliab. Election is grace, not entitlement.

themes.title: Grumblers Against Moses
themes.clue: Each challenged Moses' leadership in the wilderness
themes.explain: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rose against Moses and the earth swallowed them; even Miriam and Aaron spoke against him and Miriam was struck with leprosy. Scripture warns against grumbling (1 Cor 10:10).

themes.title: Betrayers
themes.clue: Each turned against someone who trusted them
themes.explain: Delilah sold Samson's secret, Absalom stole his father's kingdom, Tryphon lured Jonathan Maccabeus into a trap, and Judas betrayed Jesus with a kiss. Yet even Judas could have repented: no sin is greater than God's mercy (CCC 1864).

themes.title: Conquest of Canaan
themes.clue: The leader, a faithful spy, a woman who hid the spies and a man who stole
themes.explain: Joshua led Israel across the Jordan; Rahab of Jericho hid the spies and was spared; Achan's theft brought defeat at Ai; and Caleb, faithful since the spying of the land, claimed Hebron at eighty-five.

themes.title: Book of Ruth
themes.clue: A Moabite widow, her mother-in-law, a kinsman-redeemer and a baby
themes.explain: Ruth the Moabitess clung to Naomi ('Your God will be my God'), married Boaz the kinsman-redeemer, and bore Obed, David's grandfather. Boaz redeeming Ruth prefigures Christ the Redeemer welcoming the nations.

themes.title: At Shiloh
themes.clue: A praying mother, her family, an old priest and his wicked sons
themes.explain: At Shiloh, Hannah wept and prayed for a son while Peninnah taunted her; Eli blessed her, and she gave Samuel to the LORD. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas abused the sacrifices and died when the ark was taken.

themes.title: Elijah and Elisha
themes.clue: Two prophets and the people of their stories
themes.explain: Elijah faced Ahab and Jezebel on Carmel and over Naboth's vineyard; his successor Elisha healed the Syrian general Naaman, while his servant Gehazi greedily took Naaman's gifts. Jesus recalls both prophets' care for foreigners (Luke 4:25-27).

themes.title: Hezekiah and Assyria
themes.clue: A king, a prophet, two officials and an enemy spokesman
themes.explain: When Sennacherib's Rabshakeh mocked Jerusalem, Hezekiah sent Eliakim and Shebna to Isaiah and prayed; the LORD delivered the city. Isaiah 22 gives Eliakim 'the key of the house of David,' a passage the Church reads with Peter's keys.

themes.title: Friends of Jeremiah
themes.clue: A scribe and officials who stood by the weeping prophet
themes.explain: Baruch wrote down Jeremiah's words, Ahikam saved him from death, Gemariah begged the king not to burn the scroll, and Gedaliah took him in after Jerusalem fell. God provides friends for those who speak hard truths.

themes.title: Job's Friends
themes.clue: They came to comfort and stayed to argue
themes.explain: Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar sat silently with Job seven days, then insisted his suffering must be punishment; the young Elihu spoke last. God says the three had not spoken rightly of him, a warning against easy answers to suffering.

themes.title: Altar Builders
themes.clue: Each built an altar to the LORD
themes.explain: Noah after the flood, Abraham at Moriah, Jacob at Bethel, Gideon at Ophrah, David at Araunah's threshing floor and Elijah on Carmel all built altars. The altar foreshadows the Eucharistic sacrifice, and Christ himself is the altar (CCC 1383).

themes.title: Saints of July
themes.clue: Each is commemorated in July
themes.explain: St Thomas (July 3), the prophet Elijah (July 20, Roman Martyrology), St Mary Magdalene (July 22), St James the Greater (July 25), Sts Joachim and Anne (July 26) and Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus (July 29) all fall in July.

themes.title: Saints of September
themes.clue: Each is commemorated in September
themes.explain: St Matthew is kept on September 21, the archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael on September 29, and Moses on September 4 in the Roman Martyrology.

themes.title: Feasts After Christmas
themes.clue: Kept in the days right after the Nativity
themes.explain: The Church surrounds Christmas with witnesses: St Stephen (December 26), St John the apostle (December 27), the Holy Innocents (December 28) and King David (December 29, Roman Martyrology).

themes.title: Saints of May
themes.clue: Each is commemorated in May
themes.explain: St Joseph the Worker (May 1), Sts Philip and James (May 3), Job (May 10, Roman Martyrology) and St Matthias (May 14) are all remembered in May, the month devoted to Mary.

themes.title: Saints of October
themes.clue: Each is commemorated in October
themes.explain: Abraham is remembered on October 9 in the Roman Martyrology, St Luke the Evangelist on October 18, and the apostles Simon and Jude together on October 28.

themes.title: Plagues of Egypt
themes.clue: Signs sent on Pharaoh's land
themes.explain: God struck Egypt with ten plagues, from water turned to blood to the death of the firstborn, until Pharaoh let Israel go. The Passover lamb whose blood saved Israel prefigures Christ, the Lamb of God (CCC 1340).

themes.title: Churches of Revelation
themes.clue: Cities whose churches received letters from the risen Christ
themes.explain: The risen Christ dictated letters to seven churches of Asia: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. The seven lampstands are the churches, and Christ walks among them.

themes.title: Gifts of the Spirit
themes.clue: Seven gifts that rest on the Messiah and are given in Confirmation
themes.explain: Isaiah foretold that the Spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge and fear of the LORD would rest on the Messiah; the Church counts seven gifts (adding piety), given in Confirmation (CCC 1831).
